propositions: Anthropic and OpenAI usage rows with provider-prefixed model references (e.g., 'anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6', 'openai:gpt-5.4') fail to resolve in genai_prices, returning LookupError and silently dropping to unpriced state.
Bedrock usage rows with prefixed references resolve successfully while Anthropic and OpenAI do not, creating a deceptive asymmetry in provider cost comparison where only Bedrock appears measured.

The _price_row function catches LookupError at line 429 and converts failed pricing to 'unpriced' without warning, making the failure invisible except for the 'est. cost excludes N unpriced calls' footer message.
The fix must use registry membership to translate provider-qualified model identifiers to resolvable forms, not prefix splitting or literal matching, to handle edge cases like versioned AWS IDs.
All three providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock) must price correctly after the fix, verified by tests showing realistic stored rows with provider prefixes.
Genuinely unknown models must remain tolerable as unpriced without breaking summarize, but must be distinguishable in output from mis-formatted identifiers.
